bib.title: From Artificial Needles to Real Haystacks: Improving Retrieval Capabilities in LLMs by Finetuning on Synthetic Data

question: Can finetuning LLMs on purely numerical synthetic key-value retrieval tasks improve their retrieval and reasoning over long contexts on real natural-language tasks without harming general ability?
hypothesis: Skills learned on synthetic key-value retrieval transfer to real long-context tasks (MDQA, FLenQA), and an answer template lets the model learn the retrieval skill rather than the answer format.
contributions: A synthetic dataset of simple and multi-subkey dictionary key-value retrieval tasks, with an optional answer template
Evidence of transfer to MDQA and FLenQA for GPT-3.5 Turbo and Mistral 7B, mitigating lost-in-the-middle
Comparison to three long-context augmentation baselines showing less degradation on knowledge benchmarks

method.summary: Finetune GPT-3.5 Turbo (multi-subkey task) and Mistral 7B Instruct (simple task) on small synthetic numeric dictionary-retrieval sets, with and without an answer template in the prompt, loss on the answer only. Evaluate on 20-document MDQA, FLenQA (with and without CoT), general benchmarks, and against three long-context finetuning baselines.
method.task: long-context retrieval and reasoning; supervised finetuning on synthetic key-value retrieval

datasets.name: Simple dictionary key-value retrieval (synthetic)
datasets.size: 350 tasks per dataset, ~4K tokens each, 85 dictionaries with 3 to 4 keys; 3 datasets per prompting strategy (different seeds)
datasets.source: generated by authors; integer keys and values of 3 to 4 digits
datasets.preprocessing: answer-only loss (instruction masked); with or without answer template

datasets.name: Multi-subkey dictionary key-value retrieval (synthetic)
datasets.size: 150 tasks per dataset, ~4K tokens each, 49 dictionaries; 2 datasets per prompting strategy
datasets.source: generated by authors; keys are tuples of integers, subkey order randomised

datasets.name: Simple key-value retrieval, 24K context
datasets.source: generated by authors, maximum context length 24K

datasets.name: MDQA (Liu et al.)
datasets.size: 20 documents (~4K tokens); 200 samples per gold position; positions 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20; also a 120-document (~24k tokens) variant
datasets.preprocessing: also used as finetuning baseline for roughly the same number of training tokens; target answers turned into full sentences by prompting GPT-3.5 Turbo with the correct answer

datasets.name: FLenQA (Levy et al.)
datasets.size: 2000 task samples per prompting mode; 250 to 3000 tokens

datasets.name: MultidocQA, IN2, Needle-in-a-haystack
datasets.size: roughly the same number of training tokens as the synthetic data

datasets.name: MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM8K, TriviaQA, NQ-Open
datasets.size: MMLU: 20% of the full dataset for GPT-3.5 Turbo
datasets.source: evaluated with Gao et al. harness and Fu et al. codebase

training.objective: supervised finetuning on the answer part only (instruction masked out)
training.seq_len: ~3900 tokens per prompt for Mistral (85 dictionaries)
training.seeds: Mistral: 3 runs, each with different training data and seed, averaged; GPT-3.5 Turbo: 2 datasets/runs, averaged

other.trainable_parameters: Mistral finetuned on all attention layers
other.gpt_finetuning: OpenAI finetuning API; hyperparameters not given

inference.samples: 200 samples per MDQA position; 2000 FLenQA samples per mode; results averaged over 3 (Mistral) or 2 (GPT-3.5) finetuning runs
inference.prompting: FLenQA: CoT (step by step, answer True/False at end) or direct True/False. Training prompts with or without an answer template.

metrics.name: MDQA accuracy
metrics.definition: maximum subspan exact match as in Liu et al.

eval.protocol: Results averaged across finetuning runs; no significance test stated. Most results given as curves in figures.

prompts.text:
Do a task using the list of dictionaries below.
Dictionary [1] {122: 765, 4548: 1475, 4818: 4782}
...
Above is a list of dictionaries such that each key and value is an integer. Report the value of key 2931 and the dictionary it is in.
Desired answer: The value of key 2931 is 8364 and it is in Dictionary [32].
Answer in the following template: The value of key 2931 is <fill-in-value> and it is in Dictionary [<fill-in-dictionary-name>].

evidence.quote: We finetune the model for 3 epochs using OpenAI’s API.
evidence.where: Sec 3.1; App A.1 says 2 epochs for GPT-3.5 Turbo

results.claim: Finetuning GPT-3.5 Turbo on synthetic data improves 20-document MDQA at gold position 10.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 finetuned on multi-subkey retrieval, 20 documents MDQA, gold at position 10
results.quote: 10.5% improvement on 20 documents MDQA at position 10 for GPT-3.5 Turbo
results.note: Reported in the abstract; the main text gives curves only (Fig 5a).

results.claim: Mistral 7B finetuned on the synthetic data loses nothing on TriviaQA (+0.11), while the long-context baselines lose 2.19 to 6.33 points.
results.setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 ft with template vs original; baselines MultidocQA 45.20, IN2 45.44, Needle-in-a-haystack 41.30
results.note: Abstract says baseline drop ranges 2.33% to 6.19%, Table 2 shows -2.19 to -6.33 on TriviaQA (-2.43 for MultidocQA).

results.claim: Needle-in-a-haystack finetuning drops NQ-Open from 11.61 to 4.88.
results.setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 finetuned on Needle-in-a-haystack, roughly same training tokens

results.claim: Synthetic finetuning leaves MMLU of Mistral 7B essentially unchanged.
results.setup: Mistral-7B ft with template vs original
results.table: Table 1, row Mistral-7B ft (w/template), column MMLU

results.claim: GPT-3.5 Turbo finetuned without template gains 2.73 on GSM8K; with template loses 0.68.
results.setup: GPT-3.5-turbo ft (w/o template); MMLU on 20% of data; HellaSwag, TriviaQA, NQ-Open not evaluated for GPT-3.5
results.table: Table 1, row GPT-3.5-turbo ft (w/o template), column GSM8K

results.claim: Baseline GPT-3.5 Turbo gets about 0.99 accuracy on simple key-value retrieval at any gold position, which is why it was finetuned on the harder multi-subkey task.
results.quote: GPT 3.5 Turbo achieves around 0.99 accuracy irrespective of the position of gold key

results.claim: Finetuning flattens the U-shaped positional curve of GPT-3.5 Turbo and removes Mistral 7B's primacy bias on 20-document MDQA; synthetic data beats finetuning on MDQA itself.
results.setup: 20 documents (~4K tokens), irrelevant distractors, gold at positions 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20; Fig 5
results.note: Qualitative, read from Fig 5; no table of numbers.

results.claim: Finetuning with an answer template improves FLenQA with and without CoT for both models; without template GPT-3.5 CoT performance drops.
results.setup: FLenQA, context 250 to 3000 tokens, Fig 6 and 7

results.claim: Finetuning does not help when MDQA distractors are relevant (retrieved by a retriever).
results.setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 on 20-document MDQA with relevant distractors, Fig 10
results.quote: Models finetuned on our dataset will not improve in this setting, as is shown in Figure 10.

results.claim: Finetuning Mistral-7b-Instruct-v0.2 on 24K-context key-value retrieval improves 120-document MDQA.
results.quote: We observe a clear improvement over the original model as shown in Figure 9.

limits: No improvement when MDQA distractors are relevant (retrieved by relevance score), Fig 10.
Authors suggest as future work mixing the synthetic data into a larger instruction-finetuning set; not tested.
GPT-3.5 Turbo was not evaluated on all general benchmarks; MMLU used 20% of the data (computational constraints).
Most results are curves with no numeric tables or significance tests; only 2 to 3 runs averaged.
Epoch count for GPT-3.5 Turbo is inconsistent (3 in Sec 3.1, 2 in App A.1); optimizer, schedule, warmup, hardware and compute are not given.
Only 7B-scale Mistral and GPT-3.5 Turbo tested; contexts up to ~4K (and one 24K run); claim that synthetic data avoids hallucination is attributed to absence of facts, not tested directly.
Finding 6 baselines (MultidocQA, IN2, needle) sometimes outperform on MDQA or FLenQA.

terms.definition: A prompt suffix giving the answer format so that loss on formatting tokens is small and the model learns the retrieval skill rather than the format
